label: Thomas Aquinas, Summa theologiae I ii q.94…: In some hearts the natural law was so corrupted that…
locator: I-II q.94 a.5 ad 1: lex naturae in aliquorum cordibus, quantum ad aliqua, corrupta erat intantum ut existimarent esse bona quae naturaliter sunt mala; et talis corruptio correctione indigebat
interpretation: The second of the source's alternative explanations of the written law's corrective role: in some hearts, in some respects, people thought good what is naturally evil and this corruption needed correction. The formalization asserts the existence of a person and matter so evaluated, naturally evil, and needing correction. It does not assert an accomplished correction or a chronology of improved belief. The predicates for believing good, being naturally evil and needing correction remain primitive; no theory of improvement is built into their names.
